Mia (Support): Hey — customer says /v1/generate 500s and they don't see any request ID in their app logs. It's an embedded Android webview. What minimal repro/trace asks should I send them?
Sam (SRE): Quick Qs first — which environment (prod/staging), region, and roughly when did it happen? timezone helps. Also: are they using our SDK or hitting the HTTP API directly?
Mia (Support): Prod, us-west, happened ~2026-03-16 14:12 PDT, using an embedded webview that uses fetch() from the page.
Sam (SRE): Ok. Webviews often strip or hide headers. Ask them for:
  • exact local timestamp (as you already have)
  • a HAR file captured from Chrome remote debugging (preferred)
  • if HAR isn't possible, a curl reproduction including response headers (see sample below)
  • a screenshot of network request details (headers tab) if they're non-technical
Also ask them to share the full response body if possible.
Jordan (SDK): For SDK/web JS: enable verbose logs. In our browser SDK they can set `window.REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL = 'debug'` before init — that'll print request ids like `request_id=abcd1234` in console. If they're using fetch directly, the request id comes back as a response header named `x-rw-request-id` (check response headers or `fetch(...).then(r => { console.log([...r.headers]) })`).
Sam (SRE): curl example to capture response headers and body:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate -D - -o /tmp/resp_body.txt
```
Look in the `-D -` output for `x-rw-request-id:` or `x-request-id:` — that's the trace ID we will use.
Mia (Support): Non-tech friendly steps I can paste to customers?
Jordan (SDK): Short template you can send:

"Can you please:
1) Reproduce the error and tell us the exact local time (HH:MM timezone).
2) If you can open the page in Chrome on desktop: open DevTools → Network → reproduce → right-click on the failing request → Save as HAR and attach it.
3) If HAR is hard: take a screenshot of the request's Headers/Response tab in DevTools.
4) If you can run curl, paste the full output of the command below (it prints response headers):

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"<short text>"}' https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate -D -
```

We mostly need the response headers (look for `x-rw-request-id` or `x-request-id`) and the response body."
Mia (Support): Perfect — I'll send that. If they can only do mobile, include steps to forward the device traffic via a proxy (Charles/Fiddler) and export the session HAR.
Sam (SRE): One more: if they share the request id we can correlate in our logs and attach the full span/trace. If they can't get it, get the exact timestamp and customer request payload and we'll try a time-based search.
Oncall-Bot: Escalation created: INC-4521. Attach any request id or HAR to the ticket. :rotating_light:
Mia (Support): Thanks — sending to customer now :thumbsup:
